- **[adjective · advisory]** new sibling **Replicative**
  • under **Humble**
    {parent} not {child}: Research can be humble about its claims yet present only its own novel finding, never re-running anyone else's work.
    {child} not {sibling}: Replicative but not Tentative: a study can confidently re-test prior claims and report firm verdicts on which held up, without holding its own conclusions loosely.

- **[adjective · advisory]** new sibling **Corroborated**
  • under **Humble › Self-critical**
    {parent} not {child}: Research can be Self-critical (openly flagging its own limits) without ever independently re-deriving or re-testing its own central result.
    {child} not {sibling}: Corroborated checks a result against an independent method or dataset after the fact; unlike Falsifiable it need not frame refutable predictions in advance — a confirmed result can have been derived with no prior risky prediction.

## Region: Honest

- **[abstraction · advisory]** **Forthcoming** · strength 8 · regions: Honest, Transparent, Humble, Open, Rigorous
  · Caveated ↔ Documented  (Honest / Transparent) — Caveating one's own limitations and documenting one's procedures are two distinct acts of voluntarily surfacing information the reader needs, bridging Honest and Transparent under a single quality of proactive disclosure.
  · Caveated ↔ Disclosed  (Honest / Transparent) — Caveating one's claims and disclosing hidden facts are distinct acts, but both instantiate a single proactive willingness to volunteer information one could withhold, bridging Honest and Transparent.
  · Disclosed ↔ Reflexive  (Honest / Humble) — Disclosing one's interests and reflexively naming one's standpoint are two aspects of voluntarily surfacing the author's own shaping influences, so naming it leads you to expect research that exposes its own situation rather than posing as neutral.
  · Non-selective ↔ Shared  (Honest / Open) — Non-selective (withholding no results) and Shared (withholding no materials) are two aspects of one higher quality of proactively volunteering everything rather than holding back, which predicts instances that disclose both inconvenient findings and underlying data.
  · Disclosed ↔ Shared  (Transparent / Open) — Disclosing facts (like conflicts) and sharing materials (like data and code) are distinct aspects of a single readiness to make one's research contents available to others, and expecting that readiness predicts both behaviors.
  · Disclosed ↔ Non-selective  (Transparent / Honest) — Disclosing what could be hidden and refusing to cherry-pick what to report are distinct ways of volunteering rather than withholding information, bridging Transparent and Honest under a shared quality of withholding nothing.
  · Disclosed ↔ Pre-registered  (Honest / Rigorous) — Both proactively put potentially compromising information on the public record in advance — conflicts in one case, analysis plans in the other — binding future conduct, so naming the shared self-exposing commitment changes what you'd expect of the instances.
  · Disclosed ↔ Documented  (Honest / Transparent) — Both name a voluntary offering of withheld-able information — awkward ties under Honest, internal process records under Transparent — so a higher quality of proactively surrendering the optional-to-conceal bridges the regions and predicts over-sharing beyond the required minimum.

## Region: Reliable

- **[abstraction · advisory]** **Verifiable** · strength 5 · regions: Reliable, Open, Transparent, Rigorous
  · Reproducible ↔ Shared  (Reliable / Open) — Reproducing results and sharing the underlying code/data are two distinct aspects of letting outsiders independently check the work, so naming Verifiable changes what you expect — instances anyone can confirm, not just trust.
  · Auditable ↔ Reproducible  (Transparent / Reliable) — Auditable (traceable, inspectable process) and Reproducible (re-running yields the same result) are distinct aspects of the higher quality that an outsider can independently confirm the work's claims.
  · Replicable ↔ Shared  (Reliable / Open) — Replicable (results hold up on re-running) and Shared (handing over the full recipe and data) are two distinct aspects of work being independently checkable by others, and expecting verifiability predicts both robustness and disclosure.
  · Auditable ↔ Replicable  (Transparent / Reliable) — Auditable (open to inspection) and Replicable (reproduces on re-run) are separable aspects of a single higher quality—work an outsider can independently confirm—and naming it leads you to expect external confirmability spanning both transparency and reliability.
  · Pre-registered ↔ Replicable  (Rigorous / Reliable) — Pre-registration makes the analysis path independently checkable against a prior commitment while replicability makes the result independently checkable by reproduction, so both are aspects of research being verifiable, a quality that bridges Rigorous and Reliable and raises the expectation that claims can be externally confirmed.
